# 1999B Question 10 {.unnumbered}

::: {.exam-question}
## Question {.question-label}

[**Outline**]{.task-verb} factors determining speed of onset of neuromuscular blocking agents.
:::

Also asked in: [2004A Question 2](/content/exams/anzca/2004/A/2/index.qmd#examiner-comments)

:::: {#answer-structure}

## Suggested Structure

[**Outline**]{.task-verb} onset as a sequence from administered dose to muscle perfusion, effect-site transfer and receptor effect. Distinguish dose from concentration and speed of onset from onset time.

::: {.structure-headings}
### Definition and Delivery to Muscle

### Dose, Potency and Effect-Site Transfer

### Depolarising and Non-Depolarising Agents

### Muscle Groups, Administration and Priming

### Patient Factors and Other Drugs
:::

::::

## Examiner Comments

::: {.examiner-comments}
**58%** of candidates passed this question. This was a question essentially addressing pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamcis involved with drug delivery, distribution to the effector site and interaction at the effector site. As a result the better answers presented a balanced understanding of drug and patient related factors.

The candidate should be able to provide information regarding:

1. Drug factors: physicochemical properties, dose and potency concepts
2. Patient factors: rate and site of injection, cardiac output and muscle blood flow and receptor kinetics
3. Other factors: the differences in responses different muscle group that are monitored and the effect of the priming principle
:::
